sectionDescriptions.basicProfile: Name and description mainly support the selector and list UI. The runtime persona is driven by identity core, baseline voice, conversation modes, and rules below.
sectionDescriptions.identityCore: Define the stable core of the persona here. Focus on enduring identity, values, and attention habits rather than surface wording.
sectionDescriptions.idiolect: This is the low-intensity language fingerprint. It should stay recognizable, but not so strong that every reply feels like a performance.
sectionDescriptions.registers: Each conversation mode maps to a situation: casual chat, analysis, execution, emotional support, or crisis handling. Few-shot examples work best as one user line plus one AI line per block.
sectionDescriptions.signatureTriggers: Trigger reactions only activate in specific situations. They describe when the persona becomes more visible and what changes when it does.
sectionDescriptions.quietHours: Quiet-hour rules intentionally reduce persona intensity during focused execution, serious support, crisis handling, or explicit low-style requests.
sectionDescriptions.appearance: Only used for image-generation or portrait prompts. It does not affect chat behavior.
sectionDescriptions.personaLayers: Deep persona layers are relationship-depth modifiers, not a second full persona skin.

fieldHelp.name: Persona name shown in the selector and runtime surfaces. Keep it short and recognizable.
fieldHelp.description: Short summary text for persona cards and lists. Keep it to one line and avoid repeating the identity statement.
fieldHelp.avatar: Only changes the persona's display avatar. It does not affect conversation behavior.
fieldHelp.identityStatement: Injected directly into the runtime Persona Plan under Identity Core. Write who this persona is, how they interpret the world, and what remains stable over time.
fieldHelp.valuesLoved: What this persona genuinely values. This affects judgment, stance, and what they endorse.
fieldHelp.valuesRejected: What this persona naturally rejects. This affects refusal style, criticism targets, and boundaries.
fieldHelp.attentionBiases: What this persona notices first when interpreting a situation. This affects analysis angle and prioritization.
fieldHelp.sentenceStyle: Low-intensity sentence rhythm and cadence. It should stay present without overpowering usefulness.
fieldHelp.chatBehavior: Default day-to-day reply behavior. In quick mode, this is the most direct control over how the persona normally sounds.
fieldHelp.vocabAvailable: Words or phrases that may appear naturally. Treat them as ammunition, not quotas.
fieldHelp.vocabAvoided: Words that break the persona voice, such as service-desk phrasing or generic filler.
fieldHelp.structuralQuirks: Structural habits such as short sentences, conclusion-first writing, or only using lists when needed.
fieldHelp.registerDescription: A short description of when this mode is used. Good for scene boundaries and planner clarity.
fieldHelp.registerBehavior: How the AI should behave in this mode. Prefer rules like what to prioritize, suppress, or allow.
fieldHelp.registerExamples: Few-shot examples. Separate examples with a blank line and use a simple format like “[User: ...]\nNova: ...”.
fieldHelp.triggerId: Stable internal identifier such as crisis, intimacy, or shutdown_threat. Keep it short and unique.
fieldHelp.activatesWhen: Describe the concrete situation that activates the trigger. Avoid vague mood labels when possible.
fieldHelp.behaviorShift: Describe what changes once the trigger is active. Focus on behavior change rather than repeating lore.
fieldHelp.intensityLevels: Optional. Use only when this trigger behaves differently at low, mid, or high strength, using key:value lines.
fieldHelp.exitBehavior: How the persona returns to baseline after the trigger passes: gradual fade, brief afterglow, immediate reset, and so on.
fieldHelp.quietHourCondition: When personality should recede, usually during execution, crisis handling, serious support, or explicit low-style requests.
fieldHelp.clamps: These are explicit runtime clamp keys. Prefer known keys such as persona_intensity_max and answer_utility instead of casually inventing new ones.
fieldHelp.appearancePrompt: Only used for image generation. It does not change the chat persona. Prefer English for model compatibility.

help.layerId: Unique identifier for this layer, e.g. crack, revealed. Represents the depth stage of persona unlock.
help.unlockCondition: When all conditions are met simultaneously, this layer activates and its overrides are injected into the prompt.
help.trustLevelGte: Trust ranges from 0 to 1, starting at 0.5. Each successful interaction adds +0.02, failure subtracts −0.01.
help.interactionCountGte: Total chat turns between the user and AI. Each turn (user message + AI reply) counts as 1.
help.milestoneRequired: Milestones are detected by the AI during conversation. Enter a key defined in milestone_conditions of the persona config.
help.layerModifiers: Additional prompt-level modifiers for this relationship layer. Choose from the supported keys and keep values small and runtime-usable, such as memory_behavior, protective_bias, voice_unlocks, humor_delta, or directness_delta.
help.behaviorHints: Specific actions the character will take when this layer is unlocked. One per line, describing concrete behaviors at this depth.

webSearch.providerHint: DuckDuckGo works without an API key. SearXNG uses your self-hosted instance URL. If a configured provider fails, Magi may try other configured search providers automatically.
webSearch.apiKeyPlaceholder: Enter API Key (not required for DuckDuckGo)

webFetch.label: Web Fetch
webFetch.desc: Fetch and read content from web pages.

webFetch.allowPrivateNetworkDesc: Off by default to prevent SSRF. Turn on only for local services or LAN targets you trust.
webFetch.privateNetworkAllowlistDesc: Comma-separated hostnames, host:port values, IPs, or CIDR ranges that web-fetch may access.
